To say Phainon was feeling out of place, was like saying Trump's presidency was just a little unfortunate event. A drastic understatement. 

He felt… awful, actually. He didn't mind loud parties and big crowds, but this party and crowd were different. So different that for the past hour he was just leaning against a wall and stirring the non-alcoholic drink in his glass. He wasn't in the mood for drinking it, but it would be rude to just put the glass away - so he was stuck there, in this one particular motion, absent-mindedly looking at the people near him. They were all so elegant, so full of class, so aware of their movements and so precise with their steps. He couldn't really make a comment about their clothes being much more beautiful and well-made than his because that simply wasn't the case (Aglaea made sure of it), but he could complain about their toned facial expressions, their specific voices, or even the light in their eyes. Those people were the crème de la crème of current politics. 

Phainon was not. 

He held back a sigh and stirred his drink once again. Of course, a few other country leaders also decided to bring their children here, so he wasn't completely alone in his circumstances. Off the top of his head he could remember a few faceless names, mainly the queen of Castrum Kremnos and her son, Madeimos… no, Mydeimios. Mydeimas. Mydionas…

A bit of his drink spilled, creating a tiny stain on the carpet. He panicked and quickly covered the stain with his foot. 

Regardless of the name, the prince of Castrum Kremnos was still a prince. Regardless of how many siblings he had and whether he had even the slightest chance of ever being in his mother's position, he was still a prince. Someone important, who will always have that title, and who will always have at least a bit of importance. 

Phainon, as the president's son, was essentially a nobody.

Frowning at the thought, he swallowed the drink in one go and put down the glass. With his hands finally free, he scouted for an exit. A corridor, a balcony, anything leading outside of those better people… the bathroom! Perfect. 

He tried his best not to rush himself, and after agonizing twenty seconds he finally, finally entered the bathroom and quickly closed the door. He was then surrounded by a blissful silence… Well, not exactly, but compared to the ballroom with lots of people talking, glasses clinking and loud classical music played by the orchestra, it certainly felt like silence. 

After breathing a sigh of relief, he finally glanced around the room.

And saw another person.
